messages:
incident-bot: Paging @oncall — High error rate on inference runtime in us-west-2. Alert: request queue length > 95th percentile and token error spikes. Severity: P1
maya: I’m on it. seeing saturating GPUs + lots of 504s from proxy. can someone drop live mitigation options we discussed?
leo: I can flip rate limits and adjust max_in_flight from the control plane. want me to start with rate-limiting or shedding?
sanjay: Rate-limit first. Throttle public tier to 30rps per-api-key, burst 60 for 60s. Keep enterprise unchanged. We want to avoid mass failures to downstream customers.
maya: Agreed. Also reduce per-worker max_in_flight to 200 (was 600). That will shed some low-priority requests and free up KV cache.
ops-bot: Running check: current aggregated in_flight: 1,400. target after change: ~460 across pool.
leo: Applying rate-limits now via admin API:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/limits/patch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"selector":"public-tier","rate":30,"burst":60,"window":60}'
```
leo: Patch returned 200. Pushed rules to edge.
maya: Pushing runtime flags to gke/staging first, then to prod nodes in us-west-2. Config snippet:
```
runtime.max_in_flight=200
runtime.request_timeout_ms=10000
runtime.low_priority_shedding=true
```
emily: Heads-up: dropping timeout from 45s -> 10s will make some long-run requests fail; customer-support: please prep an outbound note for customers with long streaming workloads.
customer-support: Will draft. Which customers are impacted? product-ops: any VIPs on public tier?
product-ops: Two customers have heavy streaming on public tier (acme-analytics, betachat). acme has dedicated Dedicated? no, public. Reach out to their CSM.
sanjay: Also enabling prefix caching for common system prompts to reduce token generation CPU. Small config push: `cache.prefix_kv=true`
ops-bot: Cache toggle applied on half the nodes; monitoring hit rate.
leo: Observability — increasing sampling for traces to 100% for requests that hit 5xx so we can triage root cause.
maya: After rate-limit step we saw queue depth drop 40% and proxy 504s down 25%. However some workers report OOMs when shards rebalance. Increasing pod restart grace to 120s to avoid flapping.
leo: I’ll also temporarily disable streaming for non-enterprise tenants to reduce connection churn: `feature.streaming=false --selector=public-tier`
maya: Disabled streaming for public tier. This will impact UX but reduces open connections.
customer-support: Drafted message -> sharing in #marketing-drafts. will target acme & betachat with mitigation note + ETA.
emily: Any plan for traffic shaping at the LB level? might help during surge.
sanjay: Yes, adding a slowstart window on new connections at the ALB: 50% capacity for 10m then ramp. Doing that now.
ops-bot: ALB config updated.
leo: Quick sanity checks: running smoke on a sample user, observed latency back to normal 95th within 12s.
maya: Okay, next step: tune timeouts in runtime code path too. Lowering `kv.wait_timeout_ms` from 5000 -> 800 to avoid head-of-line blocking.
leo: Patch applied to runtime config; will roll on a single canary node first.
ops-bot: Canary metrics: successful for 3m. No regressions.
maya: Handing off to night oncall @leo — I need to step out in 20. Keep monitoring traces + error rate. If errors climb past 3% sustain, revert max_in_flight to 350 and re-enable streaming (but with stricter rate-limit).
leo: Ack. I’ll keep watch. setting page threshold to 1768202400 if sustained error condition.
customer-support: Notifying impacted customers now. using template: 
"We're seeing degraded performance for some public-tier streaming requests. We've applied temporary rate limits and disabled streaming; expected behavior should improve within 10–20 minutes. Please reach out if you need priority handling."
product-ops: Good message. add note about potential 10s timeouts for long requests.
maya: Final note before handoff: created rollback playbook in runbook: `rollback-max-in-flight.sh` + `re-enable-streaming.sh` with exact curl commands. Also added checklist: 1) monitor 5xx rate, 2) check redis queue length, 3) verify KV cache hitrate > 30%.
leo: Got it. I’ll run through the checklist and call if we need escalation.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigations applied (rate-limits, max_in_flight=200, streaming disabled public-tier, timeout=10s, kv.wait_timeout=800ms). Current error rate: 1.1% (down from 4.6%). Queue depth: 380 -> 160.
maya: Thanks team. leaving notes in the incident board. handoff complete. :thumbsup:
leo: Will monitor and update in 30m or earlier on changes.
incident-bot: Incident update appended to #incidents-log with id INC-2026-042."
